findings.source_quote: ἡ δὲ πύλη ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν· αὕτη μία εἴσοδός ἐστι πρὸς τὸν Κύριον.
findings.english_quote: Retain the narrated affection, sibling distinction, the Son’s role and the stated gate/name and clothing requirements.
findings.issue: The theological metadata attributes a sibling distinction and clothing requirements to this unit, although neither occurs in the selected source. This inaccurately describes the source content and the translation decision.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the sibling and clothing claims from this unit’s metadata. Describe the actual Son, gate, name, angel, and entry assertions. Also replace the associated reference to 'long editorial supplements' with a description specific to this unit’s disclosed verb insertion and conjectural readings.

findings.source_quote: ὁ μὲν υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ πάσης τῆς κτίσεως αὐτοῦ προγενέστερός ἐστιν, ὥστε σύμβουλον αὐτὸν γενέσθαι τῷ πατρὶ τῆς κτίσεως αὐτοῦ
findings.english_quote: The Son of God is older than all his creation. He became the Father’s counselor in his creation.
findings.issue: The two independent sentences omit the relationship expressed by ὥστε between the Son’s priority and his becoming the Father’s counselor. Both propositions remain, but the source’s consequential connection disappears.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: 'The Son of God is older than all his creation, so that he became the Father’s counselor in his creation.' Review this proposed wording afresh before adoption.

findings.source_quote: διὰ τοῦτο καινὴ ἐγένετο ἡ πύλη, ἵνα οἱ μέλλοντες σώζεσθαι δι᾿ αὐτῆς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν εἰσέλθωσι τοῦ Θεοῦ.
findings.english_quote: That is why the gate became new. Those who are to be saved can enter God’s kingdom through it.
findings.issue: The source makes entry through the gate the purpose of its becoming new. The simplified text removes that purpose relationship and substitutes a standalone assertion of ability with 'can enter.'
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: 'That is why the gate became new: so that those who are to be saved might enter God’s kingdom through it.' Review the replacement against the source before adoption.

findings.source_quote: εἶδες, φησί, τοὺς λίθους τοὺς διὰ τῆς πύλης ἐληλυθότας | ἀπεληλυθότας | εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ πύργου, τοὺς δὲ μὴ εἰσεληλυθότας πάλιν ἀποβεβλημένους εἰς τὸν ἴδιον τόπον;
findings.english_quote: You saw stones pass through the gate and go into the building of the tower. Those that did not enter were cast back to their own place.
findings.issue: The source asks Hermas to confirm that he saw both groups of stones. The simplified edition turns this question into two assertions, changing the dialogue’s confirmation structure before 'I saw them, sir.'
findings.suggested_revision: Restore a question covering both groups, for example: 'Did you see the stones pass through the gate and go into the building of the tower, and those that did not enter cast back to their own place?' Retain the note distinguishing the inserted verb from preserved wording, and review the proposed sentence afresh.

findings.source_quote: ἡ δὲ πύλη ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν· αὕτη μία εἴσοδός ἐστι πρὸς τὸν Κύριον.
findings.english_quote: Retain the narrated affection, sibling distinction, the Son’s role and the stated gate/name and clothing requirements.
findings.issue: Independently of the standard edition, this edition’s theological metadata incorrectly attributes a sibling distinction and clothing requirements to the selected unit.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the sibling and clothing claims and describe only this unit’s actual imagery and entry requirements. Make the associated supplement rationale specific to the disclosed insertion and conjectures here.

findings.source_quote: Ἐκεῖνοι, φησί, πάντες ἄγγελοι ἔνδοξοί εἰσι.
findings.english_quote: Retain ancient repair materials, sibling relationship and affection, gate/name requirements, holy-spirits plural and clothing imagery; preserve all substantive alternative notes.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata claims retention of ancient repair materials, a sibling relationship, plural holy spirits, and clothing imagery. None of those elements occurs in this source unit. Its angels must not be redescribed in the audit trail as a source reference to plural holy spirits.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace this copied description with unit-specific simplification decisions concerning the rock and gate, the Son’s priority and counsel, the stones, angels, and exclusive entry requirements. Retain the accurately disclosed substantive alternatives.

summary: Both editions require revision. The standard text covers the selected source without an identified main-text fidelity defect, but its metadata imports content from other units. The simplified edition independently loses consequential and purpose connections and changes one confirmation question into assertions; its metadata also imports unrelated content. The disclosed working readings and alternatives remain supportable as attributed project reports, not fresh manuscript verification. This review does not authenticate unseen images or certify exhaustive collation, and proposed replacements require fresh review.
